cover.lede: Noah, you said yes to seeing what an online presence that wins Hamburg clients looks like. Here's the plan, and the pieces already built. A new site, your Google profile, your first posts, local pages and a review card, and every one of them points to the same thing, a first conversation with you.

market.src: Statistik Nord, Statistisches Jahrbuch Hamburg 2024, table 12.8. Stormarn from Bundestag Drucksache 21/7502, annex 1, which reproduces the 2024 business register.
market.reading: So the work is rarely convincing a firm it needs IT help. Three in four already pay someone, and only one in six has an IT person of its own. Hiring one is hard too, with 79,000 IT jobs unfilled in Germany. The job is giving a firm a reason to switch, and switching takes trust a new firm has to show rather than claim.

wall.src: Each homepage rendered and read on 22 Oct 2026, and each site searched page by page for prices. FL-ITService's price sits in the PDF its footer links as “AGB”. Base2 IT Consult posts 125 € an hour on a customer notice that no menu links to, so it isn't counted here. Five of them write about documentation, none shows a piece of it.
wall.gap: Eight of them show proof you can't show yet, and four put a price within one click. None shows the thing you promise. A real piece of documentation, labelled as an example until a first client agrees to be shown, is proof a firm founded this year can show from day one.

pos.lede: One sentence a buyer remembers, backed by things they can check. The firm closest to your promise is Matic-Tec, Martin Otto writing in the first person about documented systems. He writes about the documentation. You show it.

pillars.p: Your name, your number and your photo on every page. Being one person is the selling point, not the risk.
The documentation sample on the site, the change log in your posts, the folder a client keeps.

local.lede: Firms search for IT in their own town. hagel IT, 32 people, says on its Ahrensburg page that its own team does the on site work in Reinbek and Glinde, and it has no page for either town. Six short pages, one per town, each with your face, your number and the same documented promise, put you in those searches.

deadlines.reading: Every end of support is a reason for a firm to call someone, and a moment it's open to a new name. A firm still on Windows 10 now pays Microsoft per device for fixes, 61 dollars for the first year and double that the next. Each date is a short campaign you can run, a check for the firms still on it.
deadlines.src: Microsoft Learn, the lifecycle page of each product and its yearly end of support list, read 22 Oct 2026. Windows Server 2022 only left mainstream support in October and runs to 2031, so it isn't on this list.
